::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Codebase operators only.** Every clip on this page is produced by a *registered core
operator* run through the Plexus engine — one `config/**.yaml` spec, no per-simulation code.
The interaction and boids laws are ported from
[ParticleGraph](https://github.com/allierc/ParticleGraph); the slime-mould (Physarum) agent
from [Sebastian Lague's Slime-Simulation](https://github.com/SebLague/Slime-Simulation); the
softened self-gravity from Philip Mocz's *Create Your Own N-body Simulation* (2020); the
continuum solver is MLS-MPM (Hu et al. 2018); and each strange attractor cites its originating
paper (Lorenz 1963, Rössler 1976, Sprott 1994, …). Prototype-only experiments have been
dropped — the gallery is the live operator vocabulary of the paper.
:::

Each clip below is one `spec.yaml` over the identical operators and schedule grammar;
**hover (or tab to) a simulation's title to read the exact spec that generated it.** The
first two are validated to floating-point precision against
[ParticleGraph](https://github.com/allierc/ParticleGraph). Every movie is rendered the same
way: a black-background, full-frame point splat, so the *dynamics* — not the chrome — is what
you compare across systems.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## How a clip is made
`python Plexus_Main.py -o generate_plot <config>` runs the forward simulation, writes the
trajectory, and renders the movie — no per-simulation code, only the spec differs. e.g.
`... -o generate_plot inverse_square/spiral_galaxy_3d` or `... -o generate_plot attractors/lorenz`.
:::

<h2>Interaction &amp; flocking — validated against ParticleGraph</h2>
<p class="opk">Lateral operators over a radius neighbour graph: a per-type force law (attraction–repulsion) and the three boids rules that sum to flocking.</p>
<div class="sim-gallery">
  <figure class="sim-card">
    <video src="gallery/attraction.mp4" autoplay loop muted playsinline preload="metadata"></video>
    <figcaption>
      <span class="sim-name" tabindex="0">attraction–repulsion<span class="sim-spec"><pre>op: attraction_repulsion   # lateral, EMIT=velocity
# 3 types, per-type difference-of-Gaussians law
# on a radius_graph (O(E)); byte-matched to
# ParticleGraph arbitrary_3.
config/attraction_repulsion/arbitrary_3.yaml</pre></span></span>
      <span class="sim-cap">per-type difference-of-Gaussians interaction — types self-sort into cells</span>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
  <figure class="sim-card">
    <video src="gallery/boids.mp4" autoplay loop muted playsinline preload="metadata"></video>
    <figcaption>
      <span class="sim-name" tabindex="0">boids<span class="sim-spec"><pre>ops: cohesion + velocity_align + separation
# three lateral rules; their deltas SUM to flocking.
config/boids/boids_16.yaml</pre></span></span>
      <span class="sim-cap">cohesion + alignment + separation — one flock from local rules</span>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
  <figure class="sim-card">
    <video src="gallery/active_matter.mp4" autoplay loop muted playsinline preload="metadata"></video>
    <figcaption>
      <span class="sim-name" tabindex="0">active matter (Vicsek)<span class="sim-spec"><pre>ops: velocity_align + velocity_cruise
# Vicsek self-propulsion to speed v0 + polar
# alignment on a radius_graph -> ordered flock.
config/active_matter/vicsek_flock.yaml</pre></span></span>
      <span class="sim-cap">Vicsek self-propulsion + alignment — a polar-ordered swarm</span>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
</div>

<h2>Stigmergy — Physarum slime</h2>
<p class="opk">A set + a scalar field, coupled: agents deposit a trail, the field diffuses and decays, agents sense and steer up it — a self-reinforcing transport network. One operator schedule; the network class is set by the spec (turn rate, deposit/decay, species count).</p>
<div class="sim-gallery g3">
  <figure class="sim-card">

    <figcaption>
      <span class="sim-name" tabindex="0">slime (default)<span class="sim-spec"><pre>ops: deposit + diffuse + decay + sense + glide
# 3-sensor steering up a self-deposited pheromone
# field (Jones/Lague). Stigmergy: grows, coarsens, prunes.
config/slime/slime_default.yaml</pre></span></span>

<h2>Inverse-square law — self-gravity &amp; electrostatics</h2>
<p class="opk">One <code>squared_law</code> operator, two regimes: <code>law: gravity</code> (mass, always attract, all-pairs) collapses a disc into a galaxy; <code>law: coulomb</code> (signed charge, like-repel) is a plasma.</p>
<div class="sim-gallery g3">

config/inverse_square/spiral_galaxy.yaml</pre></span></span>

<h2>Strange attractors — <code>attractor_flow</code></h2>
<p class="opk">A single lateral operator rides a whole cloud along a dissipative 3D chaotic flow ẋ = f(x); a tiny seed is stretched-and-folded until the cloud <em>is</em> the attractor. Ten systems ship; six shown.</p>
<div class="sim-gallery g3">
  <figure class="sim-card">
    <video src="gallery/attractor_lorenz.mp4" autoplay loop muted playsinline preload="metadata"></video>
    <figcaption>
      <span class="sim-name" tabindex="0">Lorenz<span class="sim-spec"><pre>op: attractor_flow, system: lorenz
# ẋ=σ(y−x); ẏ=x(ρ−z)−y; ż=xy−βz   (1963)
config/attractors/lorenz.yaml</pre></span></span>
      <span class="sim-cap">the butterfly — two spiralling lobes</span>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
  <figure class="sim-card">
    <video src="gallery/attractor_halvorsen.mp4" autoplay loop muted playsinline preload="metadata"></video>
    <figcaption>
      <span class="sim-name" tabindex="0">Halvorsen<span class="sim-spec"><pre>op: attractor_flow, system: halvorsen
# ẋ=−a x−4y−4z−y²  (+ cyclic y,z),  a=1.4
config/attractors/halvorsen.yaml</pre></span></span>
      <span class="sim-cap">a fat three-armed folded knot</span>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
  <figure class="sim-card">
    <video src="gallery/attractor_aizawa.mp4" autoplay loop muted playsinline preload="metadata"></video>
    <figcaption>
      <span class="sim-name" tabindex="0">Aizawa<span class="sim-spec"><pre>op: attractor_flow, system: aizawa
# a torus with an axial spike through a sphere
config/attractors/aizawa.yaml</pre></span></span>
      <span class="sim-cap">a banded sphere with an axial spike</span>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
  <figure class="sim-card">
    <video src="gallery/attractor_sprott_b.mp4" autoplay loop muted playsinline preload="metadata"></video>
    <figcaption>
      <span class="sim-name" tabindex="0">Sprott B<span class="sim-spec"><pre>op: attractor_flow, system: sprott_b
# ẋ=yz; ẏ=x−y; ż=1−xy   (Sprott 1994, case B)
config/attractors/sprott_b.yaml</pre></span></span>
      <span class="sim-cap">a symmetric twin-scroll with two spiral eyes</span>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
  <figure class="sim-card">
    <video src="gallery/attractor_dadras.mp4" autoplay loop muted playsinline preload="metadata"></video>
    <figcaption>
      <span class="sim-name" tabindex="0">Dadras<span class="sim-spec"><pre>op: attractor_flow, system: dadras
# ẋ=y−a x+b y z; ẏ=c y−x z+z; ż=d x y−e z  (2009)
config/attractors/dadras.yaml</pre></span></span>
      <span class="sim-cap">a swooping multi-wing bird with two eye-holes</span>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
  <figure class="sim-card">
    <video src="gallery/attractor_thomas.mp4" autoplay loop muted playsinline preload="metadata"></video>
    <figcaption>
      <span class="sim-name" tabindex="0">Thomas<span class="sim-spec"><pre>op: attractor_flow, system: thomas
# ẋ=sin(y)−b x  (+ cyclic y,z),  b=0.208
config/attractors/thomas.yaml</pre></span></span>
      <span class="sim-cap">a woven cage of interlinked loops</span>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
</div>
